newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end higher, small-cap stocks lead.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end higher, small-cap stocks lead.

text.p: Small-capitalisation stocks led the rise in Kuala Lumpur shares on Monday as retail investors continued to bargain hunt after last year's sell-off, dealers said.
They said funds were also slowly making their way back into the market, pushing blue chips higher.
"Funds are back from the year-end holidays. It will be an interesting week," said an institutional dealer with a bank-backed brokerage.
The blue chip-focused Composite Index touched a high of 1,240.11 for the day before ending at 1,233.12, up 1.67 points.

The Second Board index closed up 13.71 points or 2.31 percent at 606.54. Dealers said the index may be heading for its all-time high of 661.25 set on November 15, 1996, after breaching the key 600-point mark.
Market volume was 202 million shares against 147 million on Friday. Gainers overwhelmed losers 486 to 124.
Secondary stocks dominated the top gainers' list, led by Hock Seng Lee which jumped 3.50 ringgit to 42.50 ringgit.
UMW Holdings rose 1.10 ringgit to 13.50 ringgit. Dealers said the stock was boosted by speculation over the price Sapura Holdings will pay to take over the company.
